title: 6.2.2 Sub-build: Pull back and let go
description: One ball, one pull, one release. Set direction and speed at the moment the button comes up.

steps.title: Run it
steps.instructions: The ball sits still. Letting go of the button does nothing.

steps.title: Set the shot on release
steps.instructions: Inside `if (mouse.released())`, set the direction away from the pointer and the speed from the pull: `cue.direction = cue.angleTo(mouse.x, mouse.y) + 180;` and `cue.speed = min(dist(...), 120) / 12;`.
hints: Set direction first, then speed: speed uses the direction.
Without the +180 the ball goes toward the pointer, which is a design choice, not an error.

steps.title: Feel the power
steps.instructions: Pull a little and let go, then pull a lot: the second shot should be faster, but not endless.
hints: If every shot is the same, the speed is a fixed number.

requirements.title: The shot is on release
requirements.description: The direction/speed are set inside a mouse.released() test. Help: 6.1.2 (Reading: The pointer: press, hold, let go)

requirements.title: Power comes from the pull, capped
requirements.description: The speed uses dist/angleTo and is capped with min or constrain. Help: 6.2.1 (Reading: Which way, how fast)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch for "Sub-build: Pull back and let go". The task: set the ball's direction away from the pointer and its speed from the pull distance, capped, inside a mouse.released() test. Accept any names, helpers, ternaries and semicolons; a line only in a comment or string does not count. Short, plain notes for a 14-year-old; never write corrected code.

rubric.title: On release
rubric.description: The shot is set when the button comes up, not while it is down.

rubric.title: Direction and speed
rubric.description: Both are set; direction uses angleTo and speed uses the distance.
